themes.extreme.title: Climate Variability & Surface Extremes
themes.extreme.short: Understanding how climate variability and change drive land surface extremes and shape their predictability.
themes.extreme.description: We investigate how climate variability and change, land surface conditions, and human activities influence the occurrence, intensity, and evolution of extreme events. Our current research emphasizes fire regimes and fire behavior prediction across spatial and temporal scales.
themes.extreme.example: Global burned area increasingly explained by climate change (Nature Climate Change, 2024).
themes.carbon.title: Ecosystem Processes & Carbon Cycling
themes.carbon.short: Examining how disturbance changes ecosystem productivity, carbon cycling, and the movement of water.
themes.carbon.description: Our work connects fire disturbance to tree mortality, ecosystem primary production, evapotranspiration, and biogeochemistry. We combine observations with land surface modeling to understand these linked responses at watershed and regional scales.
themes.carbon.example: Elevated forest canopy loss after wildfires in moist and cool forests in the Pacific Northwest (Earth’s Future, 2025).
themes.climate.title: Land–Atmosphere Interactions & Feedbacks
themes.climate.short: Investigating exchanges of energy, water, and carbon between the land and atmosphere and their roles in climate variability and feedbacks.
themes.climate.description: We study how land surface processes interact with the atmosphere across spatial and temporal scales. Our research examines the effects of vegetation dynamics, land cover change, surface heterogeneity on land-atmosphere energy and water exchanges, atmospheric dynamics, and climate feedbacks.
themes.climate.example: WRF–ELM v1.0: a Regional Climate Model to Study Atmosphere–Land Interactions Over Heterogeneous Land Use Regions (Geoscientific Model Development, 2025).
